newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares close 0.5 pct up, capped at 1,140.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares close 0.5 pct up, capped at 1,140.

text.p: Austrian shares continued their recovery on Tuesday, buoyed by demand for issues listed on the OeTOB futures and options market, and the ATX index settled back into last week's 1,120-1,140 points trading range.
The index of 21 blue-chip stocks ended 5.56 points higher at 1,127.97, with 15 shares up, five down and one unchanged.
Support at 1,120 points looked secure but traders said the market may have trouble breaking above 1,140.
"I wouldn't rule out a rally towards 1,150 points by year-end but at the moment the market looks capped at 1,140," one said.
Among the session's most heavily traded shares were oil and chemicals group OMV, Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien, brickmaker Wienerberger and steel firm VA Stahl.
Wienerberger broke out of a recent down trend, rebounding 70 schillings, or 3.56 percent, to 2,065.95 schillings to become the day's top gainer.

Traders also pinpointed demand for steel firm VA Stahl and Flughafen Wien. Flughafen rose 4.2 schillings to 528.5 while VA Stahl closed 6.5 schillings up at a new year high of 394.9 on brisk turnover.
On Monday, VA Stahl reported a decline in nine-month sales but forecast a market upturn in the fourth quarter. Flughafen announced it would recommend a higher 1996 dividend payment.
The leading decliner was insurer EA-Generali which fell victim to a technical correction after recent gains. It slipped 2.2 percent to 3,560 schillings.
December ATX futures stood 14.0 points up at 1,130. The broad-based Vienna bourse index rose 1.49 points to 427.18. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
